column1: # Swapdesk key table (contract C4): HID usage <-> Windows set-1 scan code <-> macOS kVK, as data.
# Columns (tab-separated): page, usage, name, win_scan, win_vk, mac_kvk, flags, note.
#   win_scan  set-1 make code; extended keys 0xE0xx; '-' none. Keyboard-page keys are injected by scan code,
#             consumer keys by win_vk (their scan is kept for the reverse lookup).
#   mac_kvk   kVK_* of an ANSI Mac keyboard; '-' none. The rows flagged iso_swap exchange their kVK on an ISO Mac.
#   flags     comma list: iso_swap, altgr, numpad, media, jis, abnt2; '-' none.
#   [1] USB HID Usage Tables 1.5 (https://usb.org/sites/default/files/hut1_5.pdf): footnotes 13 and 16 of the keyboard
#       page name Keypad Comma for the Brazilian keypad period key and Keyboard International1 for the Brazilian /? key.
#       The usage numbers come from [2]; pdftotext on [1] garbled the numeric ID column, so the numbers were not
#       re-read there (C4: the stage-16 tests assert them against the known ABNT2 and US layouts instead).
#   [2] Chromium ui/events/keycodes/dom/dom_code_data.inc (usb, win and mac columns; it cites Microsoft's Keyboard Scan
#       Code Specification and translate.pdf, and Apple HIToolbox/Events.h):
#       (the page lists 0xC1-0xC2 as reserved: the ABNT values VK_ABNT_C1 0xC1 and VK_ABNT_C2 0xC2 are the DDK kbd.h
#       names, informative only and checked by the ABNT2 test on this PC).
# UNPROVEN until the MacBook probes (P9): the ISO swap on the owner's keyboard.
